Studio + Structure Polish — Wave 2 live-guerrilla visual verification

Task ssp-w2-visual-addendum · build 8f7489fd (origin/main after S1 #1882 + S2 #1890 merged and deployed to guerrilla) · captured 2026-07-09 on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud, 1440×900, both themes.

Verdict

The tiered / honest desk and the per-workspace enablement UI shipped by wave 1–2 are live, correct, and on-theme in both light and dark. No off-theme chrome offenders were found: scripts/studio-literal-check.sh (203 files, 0 inline color literals) and node design/check.mjs (16 surfaces in lockstep) are both green, and the styleguide token matrix renders every swatch from the generated design/tokens.json. No token-value change was required — this addendum makes that conclusion with the pixels below as proof. Two structural observations (neither a token/chrome issue, both out of S3 scope) are filed for the lead in the last section.

State 1 — the tiered desk (Default workspace)

MAIN tier holds Papers and Sheets (Bulldocs/Sheets), then Tasks and Projects; a single collapsed Plugins node; a trailing …Rest node. The Default workspace additionally surfaces Book (ONIX 3.0) + the Bokbasen group in MAIN because Default carries a saved override enabling onixedit and tickets (see State 4 — those two rows have no DEFAULT badge). This desk therefore faithfully mirrors this workspace's real enablement, exactly as the charter's "the tree never lies about the database" intends.

State 2 & 4 — Workspace Settings (the enablement UI)

The reframed /studio/settings "Workspace Settings" page: a Theme section (evergreen/ember/fjord) and a Plugins section with a per-plugin enable/disable toggle + placement selector (Main structure / Plugins folder / Top menu only) and honest copy — "Disabling never deletes content — its document types move to the …Rest folder, still fully readable." Rows carry a DEFAULT badge when at their declared default; bulldocs · main · on, frt/github/pulse · plugins · off, media · top-menu · on. Onix and Tickets show no DEFAULT badge — they are enabled here by a workspace override, which is why State 1's desk surfaces them. This is the ground-truth source that reconciles the desk against real per-workspace config.

State 3 — …Rest, the honest census

…Rest lists every document type with no placed home, with an honest total-docs count (drafts included). In Default (onixedit + tickets enabled) it holds only the true orphans bossType (1) and metric (6) — book and ticket are claimed by their enabled plugin nodes and correctly absent. Under a nil-workspace (both plugins off) the same census instead shows book (1) and ticket (1) in …Rest — i.e. a disabled plugin's types fall honestly into …Rest. The census reacts correctly to the enablement axis; force-deleted / ad-hoc public types that used to be invisible now surface here.

Plugins tier

The single nested Plugins node holds enabled, plugins-placed plugins — here Tickets (enabled via override, placement "Plugins folder"). Disabled plugins with no desk items (frt/github/pulse) contribute nothing and are correctly absent.

State 5 — styleguide token matrix

/studio/styleguide renders every registered theme × light/dark, each cell an iframe carrying its own data-bp-theme/data-theme so the shipped stylesheet fires. Palette, status (ok/warn/danger/info), paper skin and mail-chrome all resolve from the generated var(--…) block emitted by design/emit.mjs from design/tokens.json. Every swatch is on-theme in both modes; nothing hand-rebuilds a palette. This is the visual proof behind the "no off-theme chrome, no token change needed" verdict.

Off-theme chrome verdict — NO token change needed

Across all five states in both themes the Studio chrome derives cleanly from derive(theme)/design/tokens.json. No inline/off-theme color literal was exposed. scripts/studio-literal-check.sh and node design/check.mjs are green on the unchanged tree. Justified exemptions (status/traffic-light dots, TUI-preview surface, terminal panel, Mermaid configs, attribute-selector couplings) were left untouched per Decision 8. Therefore design/tokens.json and design/exemptions.json are unchanged by this slice; the merge-gated code criterion cites this section as "no code change needed."

Observations filed for the lead (structural, not token — out of S3 scope)

(A) Studio desk display is built from the ungated resolution tree. BarkparkWeb.Studio.PaneBuilder.build/3 (pane_builder.ex:46) builds one Structure.build(dataset, [gating: :none] ++ scope) and uses it for BOTH nav-path resolution AND the displayed root_pane.items. In every workspace inspected here the rendered desk still matched real enablement (Default's desk-item plugins were enabled; a fresh workspace lacks their schemas), so no user-visible divergence was reproduced — but by code inspection a workspace that DISABLES a desk-item-contributing plugin (e.g. onixedit where book content exists) could still show that plugin's nodes in Studio, diverging from the gated /v1/structure + Go TUI. Worth confirming against the wave-1 "display stays tiered" intent.

(B) Freshly-created workspace desk is schema-barren and scope-inconsistent. A workspace created via POST /api/workspaces (auto-seeds project + dataset only) opens to a near-empty desk — only the schema-independent Projects link — because the plugin schemas (paper/sheet/task) are Default-workspace-scoped, not nil-global, so list_schemas(include_global: true) surfaces nothing for it. After a first document write the scoped /v1/structure response shifted to include global schemas + a Plugins▸Tickets node, indicating the schema/enablement scope resolution for brand-new workspaces is inconsistent. This is why the pristine "clean default workspace = Papers/Sheets/Tasks, no Plugins node" pixel could not be shot in a live fresh workspace; it is proven instead by the gated /v1/structure nil-default tree (Papers/Sheets/Tasks/Projects/…Rest, no Plugins node) plus the Settings default configuration above.
